 It's a Major Recall for Honda, Toyota 
 Car manufacturers recall 1.6M vehicles over risks with Takata airbag inflators rupturing 
 By 
 Jenn Gidman 
 with Newser.AI 
 Posted Nov 21, 2026 9:30 AM CST 
 Copied 
 A Honda logo, as seen on a Honda Civic Sport Touring vehicle on display in Pittsburgh on Feb. 14, 2025.   (AP photo/Gene J. Puskar, file) 
 Honda and Toyota are pulling 1.6 million vehicles off the road over a fresh concern with Takata airbag inflators—this time in models that were previously thought to be safer due to their moisture-absorbing material. The automakers say they've seen no crashes, injuries, or inflator ruptures linked to this batch, but new testing suggests the inflators' propellant can degrade over time and potentially burst when airbags deploy, per Reuters . The recall covers about 810,000 older Honda and Acura vehicles in the US and 790,000 Toyota and Lexus vehicles worldwide, including 314,000 in the US. 
 Affected models range from Corolla and Lexus SC 430 vehicles made in the aughts to mid-2010s Honda Accords, Civics, and CR-Vs, as well as Acura models, with Hondas on the list sold or registered in hot, humid states and US territories. Since 2009, there've been at least 28 deaths and more than 400 injuries in the US tied to the Takata airbag inflators. Replacement inflators for Toyota vehicles are expected to be available by early 2027; it's not clear when Honda's will be ready. Cars.com notes that customers with questions can contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration via its website or by calling 888-327-4236.
